title: Postmortem: INC-2025-1012 Unintended model fallback in eu-west (quality regression)
author: Ava Chen
content:
h2. Summary

On 2025-10-12, Redwood Hosted API traffic in *eu-west* experienced an unintended *model fallback* where a large portion of requests were routed from the primary pinned model to a fallback variant. The fallback was *compatible* at the API level but materially different in output quality for several customer prompt shapes. This was customer-impacting and resulted in elevated complaints about correctness/formatting, plus a measurable increase in token usage.

Incident ID: *INC-2025-1012*

h2. Customer impact
* Impact window: 2025-10-12 09:17–11:06 UTC
* Affected surface: Hosted API (chat + completion) in eu-west
* Symptoms reported by customers:
** sudden changes in tone/format despite version pinning
** increased refusals on previously passing prompts
** higher latency variance (p95 up ~18%)
* Severity: Sev1 (customer-visible correctness regression, partial region scope)

h2. What happened (high level)
A routing config change intended to tighten a capacity safeguard in eu-west unintentionally expanded the conditions under which the router considered the primary model “at risk” and triggered fallback. The router then selected the fallback model variant even when capacity was available.

Primary expected model: *rw-llama-3.1-70b-2025-09-30*
Unintended fallback selected: *rw-qwen2.5-72b-int4-2025-09-15*

h2. Timeline (UTC)
* 09:17 – First elevated customer complaints in #support; no automated incident opened yet
* 09:24 – SRE sees increased “route_fallback_selected” counters for eu-west
* 09:31 – Incident declared; mitigation owner assigned
* 09:44 – Roll back router config change for eu-west
* 10:02 – Fallback selection rate drops but remains above baseline
* 10:37 – Router cache flushed for eu-west policy evaluation nodes
* 11:06 – Metrics return to baseline; incident resolved

h2. Root cause
A policy expression change in the routing ruleset incorrectly treated *transient queue depth spikes* as sustained overload. Because the router evaluates fallback eligibility before applying the per-model “pinned version preference” rule, the new policy caused “fallback eligible = true” for a broad swath of traffic.

Contributing factors:
* The canary for the routing rules did not validate “pinned version preserved” as an explicit invariant.
* Alerting existed for fallback selection rate, but the threshold and burn rate were tuned for actual capacity loss events, not policy-induced false positives.

h2. Detection
Detected by customer reports + manual metric inspection. Automated alert fired ~13 minutes after customer complaints began.

h2. Resolution
* Rolled back the routing policy change in eu-west
* Flushed policy evaluation caches
* Added a temporary guardrail: do not fallback when the primary model reports healthy capacity and the request includes strict pinning metadata

h2. Follow-ups
1) Add a canary check: “pinned model honored” for representative traffic (Owner: Ethan Park)
2) Add alert: fallback selection rate *while primary capacity is healthy* (Owner: Rishi Malhotra)
3) Update router policy review checklist to include explicit fallback invariants (Owner: Ava Chen)

h2. Related
* Jira: SUP-4187 (customer escalation that began during this window)
* Slack: #incidents thread_ts=1760260920
